findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its underlying storage/snapshots hold data in cleartext, exposing database contents to anyone with access to the storage layer or snapshots.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, dramatically enlarging the attack surface for a database holding application data protected only by a static admin password.
The master username is the well-known default 'admin', which combined with a public endpoint makes credential brute-forcing/guessing materially easier.

No parameter group setting or option enforces TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport), so the database accepts unencrypted MySQL connections; the application connects with mysqli_connect without TLS, sending credentials and data in cleartext.
The MySQL parameter group only sets character sets and does not set require_secure_transport=ON, leaving cleartext database connections permitted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance role. Compromise of the internet-facing web instance yields near-total control of S3, EC2 and RDS in the account, including data exfiltration and privilege escalation via instance/role manipulation.

The user_data script interpolates var.password and the DB username into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable in plaintext from the instance metadata service (and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, which this instance's role also permits), leaking the database master password.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an internet-facing web server; an SSRF or file-read flaw in the hosted PHP application can retrieve the instance role credentials, which carry s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* permissions.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the EBS root volume (which stores the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file) may be unencrypted at rest.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, permitting unrestricted outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control if the resource is compromised.

The security group has no description and relies on separately defined rules; combined with the publicly_accessible RDS instance, the VPC-scoped ingress rule does not actually confine access to the database endpoint.
